page: Microsoft Azure E96s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 480 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core capabilities and top-tier memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in memory bandwidth for small cached blocks and strong performance for large uncached blocks. In CPU-intensive tasks, the PassMark CPU score, extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests all rank in the top tier. Single-core performance is moderate, as shown by stress-ng single-core results in the middle 50%, but multi-threaded operations like bzip3 decompression and multi-core stress-ng are highly efficient. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top tier, alongside static web serving throughput.

The absence of local storage means all storage operations rely on external Premium Storage, which introduces network-based storage latency tradeoffs. However, the high memory density and dedicated CPU allocation offer strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe drives. The CPU features advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX, which drive top-tier prompt processing speeds in LLM inference benchmarks, though text generation speeds remain average. This hardware profile is suited for large-scale database operations, memory-intensive caching layers, enterprise applications, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
